stages.title: GEOLOGICAL CONTEXT: PLEISTOCENE, HOLOCENE AND CHANGING LANDSCAPES
stages.terms: Stone Age phases are anchored in geological time.
stages.mechanism: Explain climate as mechanism, not master cause: climate - water/biota - resource distribution - technological and mobility response.
stages.consequence: The impact of the Toba super-eruption on South Asian populations remains debated.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: thar evidence indicates more surface water during much of the Pleistocene and increased mid-Holocene...
stages.answer: The textbook equation Palaeolithic equals Pleistocene and Mesolithic equals Holocene is a useful first approximation, not a rigid law.

stages.title: HUMAN EVOLUTION AND THE SPARSE INDIAN HOMININ RECORD
stages.terms: Technically, Human Evolution And The Sparse Indian Hominin Record is analysed by relating Human Evolution to The Sparse Indian Hominin Record, then testing the relationship through Mains angle and Study link.
stages.mechanism: Correct: It refers to an archaic human population first identified through remains and DNA from Denisova Cave.
stages.consequence: South Asia has a rich lithic record but a meagre authenticated hominin fossil record.
stages.trap: Biological evolution was branching and reticulate, not a neat ladder.
stages.answer: Human evolution is included only to the extent necessary for Indian prehistory.

stages.title: LITHIC EVIDENCE GRAMMAR: ARTEFACT, CORE, FLAKE, DEBITAGE AND CONTEXT
stages.terms: Archaeologists reconstruct procurement, preparation, production, use, repair and discard from cores, flakes, unfinished pieces, hammerstones, waste and use-wear.
stages.mechanism: Archaeologists reconstruct procurement, preparation, production, use, repair and discard from cores, flakes, unfinished pieces, hammerstones, waste and use-wear.
stages.consequence: Correct: It can establish distribution, but behaviour and chronology require stronger context.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: source - core preparation - blank production - retouch/hafting - use - resharpening...
stages.answer: CURRENT: Retlapalle's published lithic analysis counted cores, flakes, retouched pieces, cortex, scars, platforms and reduction strategies, illustrating how modern prehistory moves beyond naming a few finished tools.

stages.title: DATING AND ARCHAEOLOGICAL METHODS: BUILDING A DEFENSIBLE CHRONOLOGY
stages.terms: Rock art can be approached through superimposition, style, associated deposits, pigment/accretion radiocarbon, luminescence and uranium-series methods.
stages.mechanism: Rock art can be approached through superimposition, style, associated deposits, pigment/accretion radiocarbon, luminescence and uranium-series methods.
stages.consequence: Precision is not the same as accuracy; a narrow date on the wrong event is misleading.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: relative dating establishes order; absolute methods estimate age ranges.
stages.answer: Luminescence methods are therefore especially important because they can date sediment burial or last light exposure, while ESR, uranium-series, palaeomagnetism and potassium-argon address other materials and time depths.

stages.title: LOWER PALAEOLITHIC: ACHEULIAN LANDSCAPES AND LARGE CUTTING TOOLS
stages.terms: Upinder Singh notes that Palaeolithic tools are widespread but excavated habitation sites are comparatively few.
stages.mechanism: Compare textbook chronology with newer site dates, then explain the phase through landscape, manufacture and mobility rather than a list of tools.
stages.consequence: Upinder Singh notes that Palaeolithic tools are widespread but excavated habitation sites are comparatively few.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: the old contrast based on supposed absence of pebble tools has been rejected.
stages.answer: The Lower Palaeolithic is marked by large core and flake tools, especially Acheulian handaxes and cleavers in peninsular India.

stages.title: RAW MATERIALS, FACTORY SITES AND THE ECONOMICS OF STONE
stages.terms: A factory site could also be a habitation or meeting place.
stages.mechanism: Raw-material distance can indicate direct procurement, seasonal rounds, exchange or embedded travel; it does not identify one mechanism automatically.
stages.consequence: A factory site could also be a habitation or meeting place.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: baghor II's Mesolithic lithic material was overwhelmingly waste, suggesting manufacture for use elsewhere.
stages.answer: Stone was not an undifferentiated resource.

stages.title: ATTIRAMPAKKAM AND THE CHRONOLOGY DEBATE
stages.terms: Attirampakkam is a model case for how new dates revise periodization without eliminating uncertainty.
stages.mechanism: CURRENT: The 2026 South Asian Palaeolithic symposium foregrounded precisely the problem Attirampakkam raises: transitions cannot be assumed from inherited European period bands.
stages.consequence: The site does not prove which hominin species made the tools.
stages.trap: Do not attach the transition to Homo sapiens without fossil evidence.
stages.answer: Attirampakkam in the Kortallaiyar basin is central because multidisciplinary excavation exposed a long fluvial sequence containing Acheulian and Middle Palaeolithic technologies.

stages.title: MIDDLE PALAEOLITHIC: FLAKE INDUSTRIES AND PREPARED-CORE PLANNING
stages.terms: The Middle Palaeolithic shows a shift in balance from large bifaces toward smaller, lighter flake tools.
stages.mechanism: Correct: It is a prepared-core reduction strategy that produces planned flakes.
stages.consequence: Prepared-core methods demonstrate anticipation of the desired blank before the decisive blow, though handaxes and cleavers did not disappear everywhere.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: middle Palaeolithic assemblages include scrapers, points, borers and other flake tools, with regional persistence...
stages.answer: The Middle Palaeolithic shows a shift in balance from large bifaces toward smaller, lighter flake tools.

stages.title: UPPER PALAEOLITHIC: BLADES, BONE TOOLS AND SYMBOLIC EXPANSION
stages.terms: Technically, Upper Palaeolithic: Blades, Bone Tools And Symbolic Expansion is analysed by relating Upper Palaeolithic to Blades, then testing the relationship through Bone Tools and Symbolic Expansion.
stages.mechanism: Wrong: Upper Palaeolithic means only stone blades.
stages.consequence: Symbolic evidence expands, yet does not justify reconstructing a formal religion.
stages.trap: Ornament production implies skill, social communication and non-utilitarian value, but exact identity messages are unknown.
stages.answer: The Upper Palaeolithic is conventionally associated with parallel-sided blades, burins, bone tools, ornaments and more visible symbolic evidence.

stages.title: TECHNOLOGY AS ADAPTATION: CORE TOOLS TO MICROLITHIC COMPOSITES
stages.terms: Composite tools reduce replacement cost because a broken insert can be changed without discarding the whole implement.
stages.mechanism: Composite tools reduce replacement cost because a broken insert can be changed without discarding the whole implement.
stages.consequence: It must not be read as a universal ladder of intelligence or a clean replacement sequence.
stages.trap: Miniaturization can support mobility and task diversity, not merely scarcity of stone.
stages.answer: Correct: Tool size reflects task, raw material and design, not a simple cognitive scale.

stages.title: MOBILITY, SETTLEMENT AND SOCIAL LIFE OF PALAEOLITHIC COMMUNITIES
stages.terms: Technically, Mobility, Settlement And Social Life Of Palaeolithic Communities is analysed by relating Mobility to Settlement, then testing the relationship through Social Life Of Palaeolithic Communities and Mains angle.
stages.mechanism: Mobility was a knowledge-intensive adaptation involving routes, seasons and social ties.
stages.consequence: Reciprocity and sharing are plausible in small mobile groups, but status and gender cannot be reconstructed solely from analogy.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: mobility was scheduled around water, food, stone and seasonality.
stages.answer: It is not direct evidence for every prehistoric community.

stages.title: SUBSISTENCE AND CLIMATE-ECOLOGY ADAPTATION
stages.terms: Palaeolithic and Mesolithic subsistence was broad and ecologically specific.
stages.mechanism: Kachchh shell middens preserve discarded shells from food consumption and were dated through AMS carbon-14 research.
stages.consequence: Hunting matters, but gathering, fishing, shellfish collection, scavenging, plant processing and small-animal capture may have supplied substantial food.
stages.trap: Resource diversity can support longer residence, but settlement permanence must be demonstrated independently.
stages.answer: Palaeolithic and Mesolithic subsistence was broad and ecologically specific.

stages.title: PALAEOLITHIC ART, ORNAMENT AND CULT EVIDENCE
stages.terms: CURRENT: Conservation science and direct/indirect dating remain crucial because claims about 'oldest art' are especially vulnerable to overstatement.
stages.mechanism: CURRENT: Conservation science and direct/indirect dating remain crucial because claims about 'oldest art' are especially vulnerable to overstatement.
stages.consequence: These finds show non-utilitarian behaviour but do not permit a complete reconstruction of religion.
stages.trap: Continuity with present communities can inspire questions but cannot prove unchanged belief.
stages.answer: Indian Palaeolithic symbolic evidence includes cupules, engravings, beads, unusual discs, ochre and the debated Baghor I platform.

stages.title: MESOLITHIC TRANSITION: HOLOCENE ADAPTATION, NOT A SINGLE REVOLUTION
stages.terms: Pottery is absent at many Mesolithic sites but occurs at some.
stages.mechanism: The Mesolithic record is larger and more socially detailed than the Indian Palaeolithic record.
stages.consequence: Pottery is absent at many Mesolithic sites but occurs at some.
stages.trap: Transition means changing proportions and combinations, not universal replacement.
stages.answer: CURRENT: Recent regional microlithic research in the Lower Ganga Basin treats chronology and ecology together, reinforcing that the Mesolithic is regionally defined.

stages.title: MICROLITHS AND COMPOSITE TECHNOLOGY
stages.terms: Explain why microliths are a technological system: production + backing + hafting + replaceability + functional diversity.
stages.mechanism: Do not date an undated surface microlith merely by typology.
stages.consequence: Bow-and-arrow use is plausible at many sites but should be supported by impact and contextual evidence.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: explain why microliths are a technological system.
stages.answer: Microliths are small stone inserts, usually under 5 cm, commonly made on short blades of chert, chalcedony, jasper, agate, quartz or related stone.

stages.title: MESOLITHIC SUBSISTENCE, SEDENTARINESS AND DOMESTICATION DEBATES
stages.terms: Technically, Mesolithic Subsistence, Sedentariness And Domestication Debates is analysed by relating Mesolithic Subsistence to Sedentariness, then testing the relationship through Domestication Debates and Mains angle.
stages.mechanism: Pottery and copper can enter forager communities through interaction.
stages.consequence: Some sites report domesticated animals, pottery or cultivated plants, but identification, stratigraphy and dating are frequently contested.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: thick deposits, huts, heavy grinding stones, commensal species, seasonality evidence and cemeteries can demonstrate...
stages.answer: Adamgarh domestication claims are questioned because of uncertain dates and stratigraphy.

stages.title: BURIALS, RITUAL AND SOCIAL ORGANIZATION
stages.terms: Technically, Burials, Ritual And Social Organization is analysed by relating Burials to Ritual, then testing the relationship through Social Organization and Mains angle.
stages.mechanism: CURRENT: The 2026 Ladakh aDNA study is later than the Stone Age, but it illustrates how burials can now be studied through osteology, radiocarbon, kinship and genome-wide data together.
stages.consequence: Burial is an action by survivors, not a transparent portrait of the deceased.
stages.trap: Unequal grave goods may signal social difference, but a hereditary hierarchy is not demonstrated.
stages.answer: Use burials to connect settlement permanence, social memory and ritual while distinguishing evidence from interpretation.

stages.title: ROCK ART: BHIMBETKA, REGIONAL TRADITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
stages.terms: Bhimbetka should be used as a combined history-art-conservation case: evidence of life, limits of meaning, and heritage-management ethics.
stages.mechanism: Rock art also occurs in Mirzapur, Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, Ladakh, Kumaon and peninsular India.
stages.consequence: It is an archaeological source, not a picture-book transcript.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: bhimbetka should be used as a combined history-art-conservation case.
stages.answer: Tourism can improve interpretation and funding but increases touch, moisture, litter and infrastructure risks.

stages.title: MAJOR INDIAN SITES AND REGIONAL TRADITIONS: A TEXT MAP
stages.terms: Isampur is a major manufacturing and habitation centre in the Hunsgi valley.
stages.mechanism: Site clusters should be read as regional systems connected by movement and exchange.
stages.consequence: Isampur is a major manufacturing and habitation centre in the Hunsgi valley.
stages.trap: Wrong: Sarai Nahar Rai is a Lower Palaeolithic handaxe site.
stages.answer: Indian prehistory is a mosaic of river valleys, plateaus, deserts, coasts, caves and alluvial plains.

stages.title: CONTINUITY AND CHANGE TOWARD THE NEOLITHIC
stages.terms: The movement toward food production was gradual and regionally varied.
stages.mechanism: Correct: Pottery can occur among foragers and may be acquired through contact.
stages.consequence: The Neolithic threshold is a bundle of processes, not a single invention.
stages.trap: Mesolithic communities could experiment with plant intensification, animal management, pottery, storage and longer residence while continuing to hunt, gather and fish.
stages.answer: Neolithic markers include domesticated plants/animals, cultivation, more settled village life, polished tools and often pottery, but these features do not always arrive together.

stages.title: HISTORIOGRAPHICAL DEBATES, SOURCE LIMITATIONS AND CURRENT RESEARCH
stages.terms: Kachchh research uses shell middens and AMS dating to reconstruct early coastal adaptation.
stages.mechanism: Conclude: Indian prehistory is no longer a single march from crude to refined tools; it is a regionally varied history of adaptation reconstructed through converging but incomplete evidence.
stages.consequence: Tools remain essential, but they are now integrated with geomorphology, palaeoclimate, use-wear, residue, fauna, burials, aDNA and heritage science.
stages.trap: The 2026 Ladakh study recovered genome-wide data from 10 unique individuals and demonstrates current South Asian aDNA capacity, while remaining chronologically later than this topic.
stages.answer: The central historiographical shift is from a typological culture ladder to regional, behavioural and interdisciplinary prehistory.
